title: Files on disk: the data directory (PGDATA)
one_liner: PGDATA is one folder that holds everything a PostgreSQL server owns: your table files, the write-ahead log, transaction status, config files and a control file.
analogy: PGDATA is a filing cabinet. The drawers named base and global hold the actual papers (tables). The pg_wal drawer is the diary of every change. pg_xact is a list of which jobs finished. pg_control is the sticky note on the front that says when you last tidied up.
big_picture: A cluster is one PGDATA folder. One postmaster process owns it. postmaster.pid is the lock that stops a second server from using it.
Every table, index and TOAST table is one or more plain files. The file name is a number called the relfilenode, not the table name.
Files for a database live in base/<database oid>/. Files shared by all databases (pg_database, pg_authid, pg_tablespace) live in global/.
Each relation can have extra forks: _fsm (free space map), _vm (visibility map), _init (for unlogged tables). The main fork has no suffix.
Big relations are cut into 1GB segments: 16444, 16444.1, 16444.2. The size is RELSEG_SIZE blocks times BLCKSZ (131072 x 8192 = 1GB).
Small directories hold shared state that must survive a crash: pg_xact (commit status), pg_multixact, pg_subtrans, pg_commit_ts, pg_serial, pg_notify. They are SLRU files.
pg_wal holds 16MB WAL segments. pg_control records the last checkpoint so crash recovery knows where to start replaying.
Some catalogs cannot find their own file through pg_class, so pg_filenode.map (global/ and per database) maps catalog oid to relfilenode.
Config files live inside PGDATA by default: postgresql.conf (you edit it), postgresql.auto.conf (ALTER SYSTEM writes it), pg_hba.conf, pg_ident.conf.
Signal files change how the server starts: standby.signal (be a standby), recovery.signal (point in time recovery), backup_label (a backup needs recovery).

flow.detail: initdb makes the directories from a fixed list (subdirs[]), copies the config templates, then runs the backend in bootstrap mode to build template1 in base/1, then creates template0 (base/4) and postgres (base/5).

flow.step: The postmaster takes the lock file
flow.detail: The postmaster writes postmaster.pid (pid, data dir, start time, port, socket dir, listen address, shared memory key, status). A second start sees the pid and refuses.
The server reads global/pg_control. If the state is not 'shut down', it replays WAL from the last checkpoint REDO location. If backup_label exists it starts from there instead.

flow.step: CREATE TABLE picks a file number
flow.detail: A new relation gets a relfilenode from the OID counter. Rows are written into 8KB pages of base/<db oid>/<relfilenode>.

flow.step: Path is built from three numbers
flow.detail: GetRelationPath turns (tablespace oid, database oid, relfilenode, fork) into base/5/16444, base/5/16444_fsm, global/1262 or pg_tblspc/<spc>/PG_<ver>_<catver>/<db>/<file>.
VACUUM creates the _fsm and _vm forks. Before VACUUM only the main fork exists.
md.c opens the next segment file (name.1, name.2) once a segment reaches RELSEG_SIZE blocks.
Sorts and hashes that overflow work_mem write pgsql_tmp<pid>.<n> into base/pgsql_tmp (or tablespace/pgsql_tmp). They are deleted at end of use and swept at server start.
A clean stop writes a shutdown checkpoint, sets pg_control to 'shut down', removes postmaster.pid and saves stats to pg_stat/pgstat.stat.

diagram.claim: PGDATA is a set of directories where the postmaster, backends and checkpointer each read or write their own files.

interview.q: What is PGDATA and what makes one cluster?
answer: It is the data directory. Its path is given by -D or the PGDATA env var.
One PGDATA is one cluster, run by one postmaster.
It holds many databases. They are folders under base/.
interview.trap: A cluster is not a database. Many databases share one PGDATA, one WAL and one pg_control.

interview.q: Where is my table on disk?
answer: Run SELECT pg_relation_filepath('t'). I got base/5/16444.
5 is the database oid, 16444 is the relfilenode.
The file is a series of 8KB pages.
interview.trap: The file name is not the table name. The name is a number.

interview.q: Are the table oid and its file name the same number?
answer: Often at first, yes (t had oid 16444 and relfilenode 16444).
TRUNCATE, VACUUM FULL, CLUSTER and some ALTER TABLE give the table a new relfilenode. I saw t move from base/5/16444 to base/5/16504 after TRUNCATE. The oid stays the same.
The truth is pg_class.relfilenode.
interview.trap: Do not map oid to file by assuming they match. For mapped catalogs pg_class.relfilenode is 0.

answer: _fsm is the free space map. It tells INSERT which pages have room.
_vm is the visibility map. It marks all-visible and all-frozen pages, so VACUUM and index-only scans skip them.
They appear after VACUUM. Before it, my table t had only the main file.
interview.trap: They are forks of the same relation, not separate tables. pg_relation_size(rel,'fsm') shows their size.

interview.q: What is a TOAST table and how do I find its file?
answer: Big values (over about 2KB per row) are compressed or stored out of line in a TOAST table.
pg_class.reltoastrelid points to it. Mine was pg_toast.pg_toast_16449 in base/5/16452, with an index in base/5/16453.
The name pg_toast_<oid of parent table>.
interview.trap: A table gets a TOAST table only if it has a column type that can be toasted (like text), even when no value is large. Check reltoastrelid.

interview.q: Why does a big table have files named 16517.1?
answer: Each file is capped at RELSEG_SIZE blocks, 131072 x 8KB = 1GB.
I loaded 1.2GB. Result: 16517 at 1073741824 bytes and 16517.1 at 213573632 bytes.
The _fsm fork is separate (16517_fsm), it is not a segment.
interview.trap: The 1GB size is a compile-time option (--with-segsize). pg_controldata prints 'Blocks per segment of large relation'.

interview.q: What is pg_filenode.map and why does it exist?
answer: Some catalogs (pg_class, pg_proc and others) cannot look up their own file in pg_class. That would be a chicken and egg problem.
So a tiny file maps catalog oid to relfilenode. There is one in global/ (shared catalogs) and one per database dir. Each is 524 bytes.
VACUUM FULL pg_class moved it from base/5/1259 to base/5/16507 and updated the map.
interview.trap: pg_class.relfilenode shows 0 for these catalogs. Use pg_relation_filepath() instead.

interview.q: What does global/pg_control hold and why must it never be edited?
answer: It is one 8KB file with a CRC. It stores system identifier, last checkpoint location, REDO location, timeline, next XID, next OID, cluster state, and key settings like wal_level.
Crash recovery starts from it. Run pg_controldata -D <dir> to read it.
pg_resetwal is the last-resort tool if it is lost.
interview.trap: Editing or deleting it can silently lose data. pg_controldata is read only and safe, even on a running server.

answer: auto.conf is read after postgresql.conf, so it wins.
ALTER SYSTEM writes only auto.conf. I set work_mem = '8MB' and pg_settings.sourcefile showed auto.conf.
Remove a line with ALTER SYSTEM RESET.
interview.trap: Hand edits to auto.conf can be overwritten. Also, the commented line #work_mem = 4MB in postgresql.conf is just the default, not a setting.

interview.q: What are backup_label, tablespace_map and standby.signal and when do they exist?
answer: backup_label says 'start recovery from this checkpoint'. It exists inside a base backup. In PG15 and later pg_backup_start does not write it into the live PGDATA, the backup tool adds it to the copy. pg_basebackup -R gave me backup_label, backup_manifest and an empty standby.signal.
tablespace_map is the same idea for tablespace symlinks. It appears in backups only when tablespaces exist.
standby.signal is an empty file. Its presence makes the server start as a standby.
interview.trap: If you restore a backup and delete backup_label to 'fix' a startup error, you can corrupt the cluster. It tells recovery where to start.

contributor_tips: Read initdb.c subdirs[] first. It is the shortest accurate list of what PGDATA contains for a given version.
In 20devel initdb creates pg_wal/summaries (WAL summarizer, added in 17) and still creates pg_stat_tmp. My 16.6 run had no pg_wal/summaries.
Never hard-code 'base/' or fork suffixes in a patch. Use GetRelationPath or relpathbackend from relpath.c.
Any new directory or file under PGDATA needs thought for: initdb, pg_basebackup (whether to copy it), pg_rewind, pg_upgrade and the fsync step in fd.c (SyncDataDirectory).
Backup tools skip some files on purpose (postmaster.pid, pgsql_tmp, pg_replslot content). See the exclude lists in src/backend/backup/basebackup.c.
Use pg_relation_filepath, pg_relation_size(rel, 'fsm') and pg_controldata to check your patch against a scratch cluster. Always use a throw-away -D.

glossary.meaning: The data directory of one cluster.
The number used as the file name of a relation. It is not always the same as its oid.
Object id. A 4-byte number that names a row in a catalog table, such as a table or a database.
One of several files that belong to a relation: main, fsm, vm, init.
Free space map. Remembers free room per page.
Visibility map. Two bits per page: all-visible, all-frozen.
The Oversized-Attribute Storage Technique. Stores big values in a side table.
One 1GB file of a large relation. Names end in .1, .2 and so on.
Write-ahead log. Every change is logged here before the data page is written.
Simple least-recently-used cache backed by small files. Used by pg_xact, pg_subtrans, pg_multixact, pg_commit_ts, pg_notify, pg_serial.
A point where all dirty pages are flushed so recovery can start there.
An extra directory for relation files, linked from pg_tblspc/<oid>.
The parent server process. It forks one backend per connection.

try_it.shows: The top-level directories and config files that initdb creates (use a throw-away path).
The lock file: pid, data dir, start time, port, socket dir, listen address, shm key, status 'ready'.

try_it.cmd: psql -p 54399 -d postgres -c "create table t as select g from generate_series(1,10000) g" -c "select pg_relation_filepath('t'), oid, relfilenode from pg_class where relname='t'"
try_it.shows: The path base/5/<number> and that oid and relfilenode start equal.

try_it.cmd: psql -p 54399 -d postgres -c "vacuum t" -c "select pg_relation_size('t','main'), pg_relation_size('t','fsm'), pg_relation_size('t','vm')" && ls -l /tmp/demo_pgdata/base/5 | grep -E '_fsm|_vm' | tail -3
try_it.shows: The _fsm and _vm forks appear after VACUUM.
Cluster state, checkpoint location, next XID and OID, and block size from global/pg_control.
Clean shutdown (postmaster.pid disappears), then delete the throw-away cluster.

file_tree.what: 3 bytes, the major version ('16'). Checked at startup.
Main config file, 29690 bytes, all settings commented to defaults.
88 bytes at first, only a warning comment. ALTER SYSTEM appends here.
Client authentication rules. initdb default is trust for local and loopback.
User name maps for ident and peer auth. Only comments after initdb.
Created at start, removed at stop. Lock file with pid, paths, port, status.
The command line the postmaster was started with. The postmaster writes it, and pg_ctl reads it for restart.
8192 bytes. Checkpoint and cluster state. Read with pg_controldata.
524 bytes. Map for shared catalogs (pg_database is global/1262).
pg_database heap file. Other numbered files here are shared catalogs and their indexes.
template1, the model database (oid 1).
template0, the pristine copy (oid 4).
postgres, the default database (oid 5). User tables got numbers from 16384 up.
524 bytes. Maps pg_class, pg_proc, etc. to files. Each database has one.
Version marker for that database.
pg_class heap before VACUUM FULL moved it to base/5/16507.
My table t, 1417216 bytes (173 pages of 8KB).
Free space map of t, 24576 bytes, created by VACUUM.
Visibility map of t, 8192 bytes, created by VACUUM.
TOAST table of table big (pg_toast.pg_toast_16449); its index is 16453.
First 1GB segment (1073741824 bytes) of a 1.2GB table.
Second segment, 213573632 bytes.
Temp spill files for big sorts. I saw pgsql_tmp61456.0 and .1 during a query. Empty otherwise.
16777216 bytes WAL segment. Name = timeline 8 hex, then log id and segment.
Marker files (.ready/.done) for WAL archiving.
Commit status, 2 bits per transaction (SLRU).
Multixact offsets, SLRU (row lock by several transactions).
Multixact members, SLRU.
Subtransaction to parent map (SLRU).
Commit timestamps. Empty because track_commit_timestamp is off.
Old committed serializable transaction info. Empty until SSI needs it.
LISTEN/NOTIFY queue pages. Empty in my run.
State files of PREPARE TRANSACTION. Empty, max_prepared_transactions is 0.
Exported snapshots. I saw 00000003-0000003E-1 while pg_export_snapshot was live.
One folder per replication slot. 200 byte state file. Created and removed with the slot.
8 bytes. Replication origin positions.
Logical decoding snapshots. Empty.
Logical rewrite mappings. Empty.
Dynamic shared memory files. Empty because dynamic_shared_memory_type is posix.
Stats saved at clean shutdown (80556 bytes). Empty while running.
Old stats temp dir. Empty. Still created by initdb, still in 20devel.
Symlink to a tablespace directory. Inside it: PG_16_202307071/<db oid>/<relfilenode>.
Only in a base backup copy, never in the running cluster. 227 bytes in my pg_basebackup.
Empty file. -R in pg_basebackup creates it, plus primary_conninfo in postgresql.auto.conf.
Only in backups of clusters that use tablespaces. Not created in my backup.

verified_by_running: initdb from postgresql@16 (16.6) into the temp dir exited 0. Fresh PGDATA was 39MB with 24 entries.
find showed base/1, base/4, base/5 each with 299 files; global has pg_control (8192) and pg_filenode.map (524); pg_wal had one 16777216 byte segment.
Start with -k <long path> failed: the unix socket path was longer than 103 bytes. I used -c unix_socket_directories='' with TCP on 127.0.0.1:54302 instead.
postmaster.pid had 8 lines: pid, data dir, start time, port 54302, empty socket dir, listen address 'localhost', shm key '321048693     65538', and 'ready'.
pg_database oids: postgres 5, template1 1, template0 4.
pg_relation_filepath('t') = base/5/16444 with oid 16444 and relfilenode 16444. After VACUUM: 16444 (1417216), 16444_fsm (24576), 16444_vm (8192). Before VACUUM only the main file existed.
Table big: reltoastrelid = pg_toast.pg_toast_16449 at base/5/16452 (409600 bytes), index at base/5/16453.
TRUNCATE moved t from base/5/16444 to base/5/16504 (new relfilenode, same oid).
pg_class showed relfilenode 0 and path base/5/1259; after VACUUM FULL pg_class the path was base/5/16507 (map updated).
pg_database path is global/1262.
pg_controldata: pg_control version 1300, catalog version 202307071, state 'in production' while running and 'shut down' after stop, block size 8192, blocks per segment 131072.
1.2GB table seg: base/5/16517 = 1073741824 bytes and base/5/16517.1 = 213573632 bytes.
Tablespace ts1: pg_tblspc/16513 is a symlink, relation path pg_tblspc/16513/PG_16_202307071/5/16514.
Sort with work_mem 64kB created base/pgsql_tmp/pgsql_tmp61456.0 (4200000 bytes) and .1 (12492800) during the query. Directory remained, empty.
Physical slot s1 created pg_replslot/s1/state (200 bytes). pg_export_snapshot created pg_snapshots/00000003-0000003E-1 (83 bytes).
pg_commit_ts, pg_dynshmem, pg_serial, pg_twophase, pg_notify were empty. pg_stat was empty while running and held pgstat.stat after stop.
ALTER SYSTEM SET work_mem='8MB' wrote it to postgresql.auto.conf; pg_settings sourcefile pointed to auto.conf.

pg_basebackup -R produced backup_label (227 bytes), backup_manifest, an empty standby.signal and primary_conninfo in postgresql.auto.conf. A tablespace backup in tar failed because the symlink target was over the 99 char tar limit, so I dropped the tablespace first.
pg_backup_start in 16 did not create backup_label or tablespace_map in the live PGDATA.
Server stopped with pg_ctl stop -m fast, postmaster.pid removed, whole tmp-pgdata dir deleted and no postgres process on port 54302 left.

Source checked in the 20devel repo (PACKAGE_VERSION 20devel): initdb.c subdirs[] lists pg_wal/summaries and pg_stat_tmp; relpath.c forkNames is main/fsm/vm/init; file_utils.h defines PG_TEMP_FILES_DIR 'pgsql_tmp'; xlog.h defines backup_label and tablespace_map; relmapper.c defines pg_filenode.map.
more: In Docker, mount a volume on PGDATA or the data dies with the container. Images up to 17 use /var/lib/postgresql/data; newer images use a versioned subfolder.
initdb refuses a non-empty directory. A volume root with lost+found breaks it, so point PGDATA at a subdirectory.
PGDATA must be owned by the server user with mode 0700 or 0750, or the server refuses to start.
Never copy a live PGDATA with cp or rsync as a backup. Use pg_basebackup.
WAL segment size is chosen at initdb (--wal-segsize). 16MB is only the default.
Deleting files from pg_wal by hand is a classic cause of corruption. Replication slots and failed archiving make it grow.
